correctness.rationale: The ordinary (not total) three-cut complex has facets complements of disconnected triples. The combinatorial Alexander dual is the clique-completion of connected induced triples in H(3,3). Independently enumerated all 27 coordinate triples and all 351 edges, 351 connected triangles, 81 rectangular tetrahedra and no higher faces; the precise dual f-vector is (27,351,351,81). Independently reconstructed signed integral triangle boundaries on the 325-dimensional K27 cycle lattice, obtaining a fully terminating unimodular unit-column reduction of rank 217, with 134 free columns. Independently reduced 81 tetrahedral boundaries in those kernel coordinates with 81 unit pivots and no residual; thus H1(dual)=Z^108 and H2(dual)=Z^53, no torsion, H3=0. Integral combinatorial Alexander duality on 27 vertices sends H^1(dual) to H23(cut) and H^2(dual) to H22(cut); universal coefficients have no Ext. Every cut facet has 24 vertices (dimension 23), and nonzero H22 obstructs pure shellability. All numbers are an exact finite computation, not inference from mod-p rank.

originality.rationale: The exact single-graph integral homology pair and nonshellability for ordinary Δ3(H(3,3)) were not identified in the directly examined relevant papers or published findings. Prior statements about the binary cube, two-factor rook graph, ordinary path-grid graph and Rips/neighbor complexes concern different graphs or different face predicates. value.rationale: H(3,3)=K3□K3□K3 is the smallest nonbinary three-coordinate Hamming graph, a canonical symmetric test of ordinary cut topology. Two adjacent nonzero torsion-free homology degrees and a nonshellability obstruction are structurally different from the one-degree two-factor rook classification. An exact reproducible integral invariant of this natural graph is independently useful even without a uniform family theorem.

scientific_limitations: Only H(3,3), ordinary Δ3; no parameter-general homotopy classification.
Exact rank/cokernel checks are finite integer algorithms and cannot certify a different graph or a generalized homotopy equivalence.
